headline: RBI: UNSC removes 3 entries from ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida list; REs to act under UAPA s.51A
summary_points: UNSC (press release SC/16488, Oct 26, 2026) removed three entries from the ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List, as informed by MEA.
Asset freeze, travel ban and arms embargo under UNSC resolution 2734 (2024) no longer apply to these names.
REs must act per Chapter IX of the RBI KYC Directions, 2025 and the UAPA Order of February 02, 2021 (amended April 22, 2024).

rows: Syrian Arab Republic / State of Palestine

who_is_affected: Banks, SFBs, payment banks, co-operative banks, RRBs, LABs, NBFCs, ARCs and AIFIs, which must screen customers against UNSC sanctions lists.
action_required: Update sanctions screening lists to reflect the removal of the three entries and follow Chapter IX of the KYC Directions and the UAPA Order procedure; forward any delisting requests to MHA (JS, CTCR).

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued circular RBI/2026-27/301 on the implementation of Section 51A of the UAPA, 1967, following an update to the UNSC's ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List.

Key points:

• Based on UNSC press release SC/16488 dated October 26, 2026, three entries (QDi.338, QDi.399 and QDi.400) have been removed from the list.

• The asset freeze, travel ban and arms embargo under resolution 2734 (2024) no longer apply to these names.

• Regulated entities, including banks, NBFCs, ARCs and AIFIs, must take appropriate action under Chapter IX of the RBI KYC Directions, 2025 and the UAPA Order dated February 02, 2021 (as amended).

• Any delisting request received by a bank is to be forwarded electronically to the Joint Secretary (CTCR), MHA.

Compliance and AML teams should refresh their screening databases promptly so that sanctions lists stay current.

Please verify the details with the official RBI circular before acting.
